subject: biochemistry
title: Lysosomal storage disorders: sphingolipidoses and mucopolysaccharidoses

steps.tx: Lysosomes degrade complex glycolipids, glycosaminoglycans, and glycoproteins through acid hydrolases. Inherited enzyme deficiencies lead to progressive substrate accumulation within lysosomes, cellular swelling, and organ dysfunction. **Sphingolipidoses** involve defective turnover of sphingomyelins and gangliosides, primarily affecting macrophage-rich reticuloendothelial organs and the central nervous system. Most exhibit autosomal recessive inheritance, with **Fabry disease** and Hunter syndrome being prominent X-linked exceptions.
steps.say: Lysosomes rely on acid hydrolases to break down complex macromolecules. In sphingolipidoses, defective enzymes cause progressive lipid accumulation in macrophages and neurons. Most are autosomal recessive, except for X linked Fabry disease and Hunter syndrome.

steps.tx: **Gaucher disease** is the most common sphingolipidosis, caused by deficient **glucocerebrosidase** (beta-glucosidase) and accumulation of glucocerebroside. Engorged macrophages form **Gaucher cells** with characteristic crumpled tissue-paper cytoplasm. Clinical findings include massive hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia from marrow infiltration, bone pain, and **Erlenmeyer flask deformities** of distal femora. Type 1 is non-neuropathic and responds favorably to recombinant enzyme replacement therapy with imiglucerase.
steps.say: Gaucher disease results from glucocerebrosidase deficiency, leading to lipid laden macrophages with crumpled tissue paper appearance. Patients develop huge splenomegaly, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, bone crises, and Erlenmeyer flask deformities. Type 1 responds well to enzyme replacement.

rows: Supportive care, marrow transplant in selected types

steps.tx: **Niemann-Pick disease** results from **sphingomyelinase deficiency**, accumulating sphingomyelin in reticuloendothelial cells and neurons. It produces foamy histiocytes, hepatosplenomegaly, neurodegeneration, and a **cherry-red macular spot**. **Tay-Sachs disease** involves **hexosaminidase A deficiency**, accumulating GM2 ganglioside. Tay-Sachs displays progressive neurodegeneration, developmental regression, hyperacusis, and a cherry-red macular spot, but notably **lacks hepatosplenomegaly**, distinguishing it clinically from Niemann-Pick.
steps.say: Both Niemann-Pick and Tay-Sachs present with neurodegeneration and a cherry-red spot at the macula. Niemann-Pick is caused by sphingomyelinase deficiency and features foamy cells with hepatosplenomegaly. Tay-Sachs involves hexosaminidase A deficiency and has no hepatosplenomegaly.

steps.tx: **Fabry disease** is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by **alpha-galactosidase A deficiency**, leading to ceramide trihexoside accumulation. Early manifestations include burning **acroparaesthesias**, angiokeratomas in bathing-trunk distribution, and hypohidrosis. As glycosphingolipids deposit within vascular endothelium, adults develop progressive **proteinuria, renal failure**, left ventricular hypertrophy, and premature strokes. Enzyme replacement therapy with agalsidase halts renal and cardiac decline.
steps.say: Fabry disease is an X linked disorder of alpha galactosidase A, accumulating ceramide trihexoside. Adolescents suffer burning neuropathic extremity pain, angiokeratomas, and decreased sweating. Adults face premature renal failure, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and stroke.

nodes.label: Progressive renal failure, cardiac hypertrophy, stroke

steps.tx: Mucopolysaccharidoses impair glycosaminoglycan breakdown, accumulating heparan sulfate and dermatan sulfate. **Hurler syndrome (MPS I)** is autosomal recessive due to **alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency**, causing gargoyle facial features, corneal clouding, hepatosplenomegaly, dysostosis multiplex, and intellectual disability. **Hunter syndrome (MPS II)** is X-linked recessive due to **iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency**. Hunter presents with aggressive behavior and similar physical features but characteristically **lacks corneal clouding**.
steps.say: Mucopolysaccharidoses stem from defective glycosaminoglycan breakdown. Hurler syndrome involves alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency, causing coarse facial features, severe corneal clouding, and mental disability. Hunter syndrome is X-linked, involves iduronate sulfatase, and lacks corneal clouding.
